items.title: SC Collegium recommends 9 lawyers for appointment as J&K and Ladakh High Court judges; drops former AG's name
items.summary: The Supreme Court Collegium has recommended the appointment of nine lawyers, including a woman, as judges of the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. The decision was taken during the Collegium meeting held on October 29, Thursday. As per the Collegium statement published on the Supreme Court website, the persons recommended for appointment are: - Vishal Sharma; - Vikram Kumar Sharma; - Namgyal Wangchuk; - Pawan Kumar Kundal; - Tahir Majid Shamsi; - Tabasum Zafar; - Amit Gupta; - Pranav Kohli; - Anupam Raina. Among the nine, advocates Namgyal Wangchuk hails from Ladakh, giving representation to the Union Territory in the proposed judicial appointments. The inclusion of advocate Tabasum Zafar is also noteworthy. If her appointment is formally cleared, she would become the first Kashmiri woman lawyer to be appointed as a judge of the High Court. The High Court Collegium , headed by the then Chief Justice Arun Palli, had recommended eleven names in April 2026, comprising ten advocates under the Bar quota and one judicial officer under the bench quota. items.title: Bombay High Court grants ₹2 lakh compensation to Arun Ferreira for illegal arrest outside Nagpur jail in 2011
items.summary: The Nagpur bench of the Bombay High Court has held the September 2011 re-arrest of activist Arun Thomas Ferreira illegal and directed the State of Maharashtra to pay him ₹2 lakh in compensation. [Arun Thomas Ferreira v. State of Maharashtra & Ors.] Ferreira is also one of the accused in the Bhima Koregaon case of 2018 and is presently out on bail. In a judgment delivered on October 27, the Court slammed the police for branding Ferreira as 'absconding' while he was detained in jail, and held that the arrest in 2011 in an unmarked car violated constitutional safeguards. A division bench of Justices Urmila Joshi-Phalke and Raj D Wakode ruled that police violated Ferreira's fundamental rights under Articles 21 (right to liberty) and 22 (protection against arrest and detention) of the Constitution and censured the police officers. “When the police persons are violator of the law whose primary responsibility is to protect the law, the punishment for such violation has to be proportionately stringent so as to have effective deterrent effect and instill confidence in the society,” the court said. items.title: Raise public awareness through ads on Diwali without crackers; involve Virat Kohli: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday said it was not inclined to impose a complete ban on firecrackers but warned authorities that failure to enforce existing restrictions could force it to take a harsher stand [Arjun Gopal and Others v. Union of India and Others] Importantly, the Court stressed the need to raise public awareness through print and television campaigns encouraging people to celebrate Diwali without firecrackers.The Bench suggested involving prominent personalities, including cricketer Virat Kohli, in these efforts. “ You can take help from celebrated cricketers like Virat Kohli or somebody. You can request him to make a segment that let us make this Diwali as one that is enjoyable. Let us enjoy the spirit of the festival of light, ” the Court said. A Bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale said its orders regulating firecracker use would become a “mockery” if they are not enforced on the ground. “ We also understand the sentiment of the public. items.title: After Theni jailbreak, Tamil Nadu DGP Prisons Sandeep Rai Rathore transferred
items.summary: The Tamil Nadu government has transferred Director General of Police (Prisons) Sandeep Rai Rathore, two days after 17 undertrial prisoners escaped from the Thekkampatti sub-jail in Theni district in a major security breach. All 17 prisoners have since been apprehended following a 43-hour search operation. Rathore has now been posted as Director General of Police and Chief Vigilance Officer at TANGEDCO in Chennai. K Shankar, Additional Director General of Police (ADGP), Enforcement Bureau-CID, has been appointed as the new ADGP of Prisons and Correctional Services, according to a government order signed by Principal Secretary A Karthik on Thursday, October 29. Shankar, who is due for elevation to the rank of DGP in January 2027, has previously served in the prisons department as ADGP. Rathore's transfer came a day after police arrested the final two fugitives, identified as Tirupathi and Meenakshisundaram, bringing the search operation to an end. The jailbreak took place around 10 pm on Monday, October 26, when the inmates allegedly staged a fake medical emergency to overpower prison staff.
